## The problem

Landfilled compostable waste emits methane, a greenhouse gas far more potent
than CO₂ over the short term. That same methane, captured, is renewable energy.
The question was whether a practical digester design could make capture more
efficient.

## What I built

For my award-winning Honors thesis, I designed and built a novel anaerobic
biogas digester featuring a dual-motor agitation system and multi-stage gas
scrubbing.

- Demonstrated approximately **88–94% CH₄ purity** in captured biogas.
- Achieved a roughly **35% biogas-yield improvement** attributable to
  agitation.
- Estimated statewide potential of ~30.3 million MWh of renewable natural gas
  and ~81,766 tons of avoided CH₄ emissions.

This earned the PSU Honors College Thesis Achievement Award.

## Why it matters

It's a concrete example of the stewardship principle that drives my work:
turning a pollution problem into an energy solution, backed by measured results
rather than good intentions.
